class_guess: Nested binary counters of toggling defect walls in a period-5 sea, with engine-dissolving epochs (multi-region)
summary: Period-5 sea swept by a zig-zag head; defect walls toggle like binary counters; the global epoch law is unknown
mechanism: Sea and walls: the tape is mostly the period-5 sea 11100. Right sweeps (B) shift every block 2 cells right and left sweeps (C) shift it back, 7 steps per block. The head turns only at 2-state defect walls. A right-wall bit is the insert 000 (= 0), which reflects a right sweep and becomes 100 (= 1); 100 lets the sweep through and is reset on the way back. Left-wall bits (gap-1 vs run-2) do the same to left sweeps. So the central engine drives a binary counter on each side (counter laws hold on 33,140/33,140 and 5,545/5,545 orbit turns).

Above that it is not understood. Counter overflows feed a second engine/counter pair at the right end and a structure at the left edge. Up to 2.73e9 the inner engine keeps dissolving (43 epochs between 1e9 and 2.73e9, 29e6 to 56e6 steps apart): a wall walks left one block per bounce, eating a 4/5-density sea (11110) back into 11100, and then the engine re-forms. After 2.73e9 there are none in the inner region. Each edge visit adds 3 cells (2,021 cells at 1e10), and edge visits keep slowing down.

Halting: every halt is C reading 0 just before 110 (rule H), for example a right sweep meeting B> 1^n 0 1 0, or a D sweep meeting 110. Neither is seen to 1e10. Cryptid check: nothing Collatz-like. Everything observed is binary counting or linear drift, but the unknown epoch/bit-creation law could still hide parity branching.

history.skeleton: span lo..hi of the visited tape; drift = wall-walk runs so far (8+ left turns in a row, each 5 cells left of the last; one epoch can give 2-3 runs)

rules.name: S_R  right sweep over the sea
rules.cases: any n >= 1, random 12-cell contexts on both sides

rules.name: S_L  left sweep over the sea
RB0  right bit 0 reflects, becomes 1
rules.cases: n >= 1; the turn and the start of the return sweep

rules.name: RB1  right bit 1 passes the sweep
RB1r  return sweep resets a passed bit
rules.cases: n >= 1; together RB1 then RB1r take bit 1 -> 0

rules.name: LB0  left bit 0 (gap 1) reflects, becomes run 2
rules.cases: n >= 1, constructed context. The pass-through case (left bit 1) depends on the phase of the sea on its right and is not yet an exact rule

rules.name: D_R  D sweep: 3/5 sea -> 4/5 sea
rules.cases: any n >= 1. A block 110.. instead of 111.. makes F read 0, which halts

rules.name: H  the only way to halt
rules.cases: C0, D1, A1, then F reads 0. F is entered only by A1, A only by D1 and D only by C0, so every halt has this form (200 random contexts per direction)

rules.name: CR  inner right counter = binary +1
rules.from: bits b0..b7 = inserts 000 (0) / 100 (1) in the 11100 sea (cells 680..875 at 1e9); a right sweep leaves the engine
rules.to: turns at the first 0 bit j; bits < j become 0 and bit j becomes 1
rules.cases: real orbit, steps 1e9..1.03e9: every right turn in cells 600..900 after a left turn left of cell 600; 33,139/33,139 next states are exact +1. Depth counts 16,634 / 8,318 / 4,158 / 2,080 / 1,040 / 520 / 260 / 130

rules.name: CL  inner left counter = binary +1
rules.from: 4 low bits in cells 315..435: run-2 defect (1) / gap-1 defect 3 cells right (0)
rules.to: turns at the first 0 bit; lower bits -> 0, that bit -> 1
rules.cases: real orbit, steps 1e9..1.01e9, every left turn after a right turn right of the zone; 5,371/5,371 exact +1; 346 carries past bit 3

rules.name: EP  engine-dissolving epochs (open)
rules.to: the engine dissolves; a wall walks left 5 cells per bounce, eating the 11110 sea; the engine re-forms further left
rules.cases: Wall-walk detector (8+ left turns in a row, each 5 cells left of the last): 136 runs from 5e5 to 2.73e9. Between 1e9 and 2.73e9 they form 43 epochs, 2.9e7 to 5.6e7 steps apart. 5 runs near the right end (3.7e9..4.6e9), none after that to 1e10. No exact rule yet

template.note: Nearest proved machines by table (2 cells away): a CPS_LRU_v3 certificate (this one; it stops growing at 124 cells by 1e8), CPS_LRU_v4 and RWL_mod_v1. All three are decider certificates, not structural proofs. The targeting row's verify/CounterCmp_v1.v (TM1) compares two unary counters, which is a different mechanism. Kill #12's recursive run-length counter is the closest kill in spirit, but its tape is runs of 1s, not a period-5 sea with toggling walls. No template applies.

strategy: Not ready for a proof. Next: (1) an exact catalogue of every wall shape in both sea phases; (2) an abstract walls-and-counters simulator checked against the TM to 1e10; (3) the epoch and bit-creation law, plus an invariant that rules out C reading 0 before 110 (B> 1^n 0 1 0, D> 110).
risks: Several levels: two engine/counter pairs, edge structures and engine-dissolving epochs; the regime changed at ~2.7e9, so 1e10 steps may not show every regime.
The defect algebra has real halting routes (B> 1^n 0 1 0, D> 110), so non-halting needs a global invariant on defect shapes, not just the counter laws.
Nobody has simulated it to 1e14 (sheet). qsim does not accelerate it (block size 1, 0 rules by 5.4e6 steps), and direct simulation of the growing gaps between edge visits is slow.
